entrypoints.summary: An arbitrary user submits a transaction to an attacker-controlled smart contract, which makes a non-top-level call to the Botanix mint contract.

affected_components.role: The report identifies a top-level transaction destination predicate as gating mint-contract validation.

code_slices.fixed: The report states that PR #638 removes the top-level mint-contract-address check and performs validation for every call emitting mint-contract events.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The validation routine is described as ensuring mint-contract calls have valid peg-in proofs; an invalid proof causes the receiver balance to be decremented again.
code_slices.vulnerable: After successful execution, execute_state_transitions() calls botanix_mint_contract_checks() only if transaction.to() equals MINT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS.

preconditions: The attacker can submit a transaction to an attacker-controlled smart contract.
That contract can make a nested call to mint().

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Outer transaction destination differs from the mint contract; inner contract call invokes mint().
trigger_steps.summary: Submit an outer transaction addressed to the attacker-controlled contract; have it invoke the mint contract through a nested mint() call so the outer destination predicate does not select validation.

mitigations.concept: validate all mint-contract Mint and Burn events regardless of outer destination

sources.concept: nested mint-contract call through attacker-controlled contract

impact.affected_asset: BTC represented by the Botanix minting/bridge system and, for nested burns, Bitcoin L1 token release.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause minting without a valid peg-in proof by invoking mint() through an attacker-controlled smart contract.
impact.security_effect: Unbacked BTC minting; the report also identifies stuck BTC for unprocessed nested burns.

causal_trace.summary: A user routes a transaction through an attacker-controlled smart contract that performs a nested mint() call rather than making the mint contract the outer transaction destination.

The state-transition hook invokes botanix_mint_contract_checks() only when successful transaction.to() equals MINT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS; a nested mint has a different outer destination and therefore skips peg-in-proof verification.
The nested mint effect is accepted without the validation routine that checks whether its peg-in proof is valid.
The report states that this permits an arbitrary user to mint BTC without a valid peg-in proof; analogous nested burn calls are not processed and can leave BTC stuck without Bitcoin L1 token release.

failure.operation: Conditional invocation of botanix_mint_contract_checks() after successful execution only when transaction.to() equals MINT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS.

primary_invariant.statement: Every call producing a minting-contract Mint event must be validated for a valid Bitcoin peg-in proof, independent of whether the mint contract is the transaction's top-level destination.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Validation is gated by the outer transaction.to() address instead of covering Mint events produced by nested calls.

quality.review_notes: The primary audit report supplies the finding-level control-flow condition, attacker scenario, stated impact, recommendation, and a report-only statement that PR #638 implemented the fix. The bundle contains no inspectable source snapshot, PR diff, regression test, transaction trace, or execution result; remediation is therefore recorded only at the report-stated semantic level and reproducibility is not established.

remediation.invariant_restored: Validate every call that emits Mint or Burn events from the minting contract regardless of the original transaction destination.
